newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends firmer on U.S. inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends firmer on U.S. inflation news.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended firmer at C$1.3965 (US$0.7161) on Tuesday from this morning's open of C$1.3979 (US$0.7153) and a two-year low on Monday at C$1.4000 (US$0.7142) after U.S. inflation data eased speculation about higher interest rates, dealers said.
* The U.S. government reported a 0.1 percent rise in the March consumer price index, compared to forecasts of 0.2 percent.

The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points on March 25, sparking a surge in the strength of the U.S. dollar and placing downward pressure on the Canadian currency. Analysts said that fears of another U.S. interest rate hike pushed investors to sell the Canada dollar in the past month.
Traders said they expected the currency to trade in a narrow range overnight after its slight rally on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 1.2358 marks from Monday's close of 1.2309 marks and rose to 90.31 yen from Monday's 90.19 yen.
